name: Purdue University
character: Situated near the western bank of the Wabash River, the campus is divided by Mitch Daniels Boulevard with academic buildings, malls, athletic facilities, and underground tunnels.

landmarks.name: Purdue Mall
landmarks.quote: The Purdue Mall is the central quad of Purdue University and was created to connect the academic campus with Ross-Ade Stadium.
landmarks.look: A central campus quad featuring a 38-foot-tall concrete fountain.

landmarks.name: Purdue Bell Tower
landmarks.quote: The Purdue Bell Tower is between the Stadium and Centennial Malls.
landmarks.look: An iconic university bell tower standing between two campus malls.

landmarks.name: University Hall
landmarks.quote: University Hall is the only building remaining from the original six-building campus.
landmarks.look: A historic 1870s university hall facing Memorial Mall.

landmarks.name: Ross-Ade Stadium
landmarks.quote: Many of Purdue's athletic facilities are there, including Ross–Ade Stadium (American football)
landmarks.look: A large collegiate American football stadium.

landmarks.name: Purdue Memorial Mall
landmarks.quote: The Purdue Memorial Mall, south of the Purdue Mall, is the original section of campus.
landmarks.look: An open campus quad surrounded by academic and cultural buildings.

landmarks.name: Edward C. Elliott Hall of Music
landmarks.name_en: Edward C. Elliott Hall of Music
landmarks.quote: Southwest of the Stadium Mall is the Edward C. Elliott Hall of Music, one of the largest proscenium theaters in the world.

landmarks.name: Felix Haas Hall
landmarks.quote: Near this section of campus is Felix Haas Hall, which was constructed in 1909 as Memorial Gymnasium
landmarks.look: An early 20th-century academic hall originally built as a gymnasium.

landmarks.name: Horticulture Gardens
landmarks.quote: This area also includes the Krannert School of Management, Horticulture Gardens, Discovery Park, Lyles Porter Hall and the Purdue Airport.
landmarks.look: Plain cultivated university gardens on the south side of campus.
